evidence: Type inventory of the frozen task (grep of type= in tests/*/*/judge.toml): gates render (1) and constraints (1) are binary with all_pass aggregation; functional 16/16 binary; polish 5/5 binary; visual 4/4 likert points=5. This is the same shape as the frozen template (template visual = 6 likert points=5 with 0-5 anchors; template polish = binary), so the shipped format is followed and per SKILL.md line 65 / quality-checks.md line 170 the presence of likert is not a defect despite the internal workbook annotation (Internal Quality Checks E42). (1) Pass/fail behaviours are binary: every functional criterion is a behavioural pass/fail bar (walls, retention, holds, stale edit, idempotent send, unread, transcript, persistence) with explicit 'Fails if' clauses (e.g. functional judge.toml line 151); none asks for degree-of-quality. Gates are binary as required by check-scoring-policy. Polish criteria are observable thresholds: timer_label (setting beside title without opening a menu; public basis walls-and-retention.md line 23), hold_mark (visible without hover; line 29), phone_matter (documentElement.scrollWidth equals viewport width, box reachable), refusal_in_place (reason in words next to form, persists ~10 s; public basis line 37), transcript_print (conjunctive document-form check). These are naturally yes/no. (2) Craft is likert with described anchors at every level: visual matter_sidebar, retention_marks, transcript_page, phone_chambers (visual judge.toml lines 20-82) each give a distinct written anchor for 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 and 0. visual/prompt.md lines 28-36 define the 0-5 integer scale, forbid fractions, and explicitly reconcile RewardKit's generic '1 to 5' hint, identical to the template wording. The 0 anchors are reserved for absent surfaces, giving graceful gradation rather than all-or-nothing. Counterexample attempts: (a) broken app that could pass: an app with an unstyled matter list or raw-dump transcript cannot reach the top anchors (anchor 1 'an unstyled list' / 'a raw dump'), and functionality cannot be farmed via likert because the visual prompt (lines 10-16) restricts scope to presentation and the functional floor (scoring.toml floors functional=0.05) applies; (b) conforming alternative that could fail from type choice: a correct transcript with slightly long lines could lose the whole binary transcript_print point while visual transcript_page grades the same craft on a gradient. 'comfortable line length' is a soft craft judgement inside a binary bar; however it is one conjunct of a document-form threshold, weight 1.0 in a 0.2-weight dimension, and the gradated quality is separately captured by the likert transcript_page, so this does not amount to lost gradation of a craft criterion. No likert block is missing anchors and no craft-only criterion is binary-only.
notes: Cross-row observations for the owner (not row-41 defects): polish transcript_print's conjunct 'replies visibly indented under their parents' and visual transcript_page's 'comfortable reading width' are not stated verbatim in the brief (walls-and-retention.md line 35 says only 'in their threads' and 'a plain reading page'); assess under hidden-requirement rows (6/27/31). transcript_print and visual transcript_page grade overlapping observables (line length/document form); assess under row 28 (no double grading).
